sources.title: The Anisoplanatic Point Spread Function in Adaptive Optics
sources.venue: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific 118, 885-900
sources.access_status: not accessible during implementation (network policy); neither abstract nor full text read
locators_used: Section 2.2-2.3: differential (anisoplanatic) phase and its structure function, Eq. 12
Eq. 5: long-exposure OTF as the telescope OTF times exp(-D/2) of the residual structure function
Figure 1: structure function along baselines parallel and perpendicular to the offset
Figure 2: Strehl versus separation, ideal-correction calculation against the isoplanatic-angle approximation

equation_as_used.residual: eps_theta(r) = sum_l [S_l(r + h_l theta) - S_l(r)] (ideal on-axis correction of every layer, thin layers, zenith)
equation_as_used.structure_function: D_eps(rho) = sum_l [2 D_l(rho) + 2 D_l(h_l theta) - D_l(rho + h_l theta) - D_l(rho - h_l theta)], D_l the single-layer phase structure function
equation_as_used.otf: OTF_LE(rho) = OTF_tel(rho) exp(-D_eps(rho)/2); on-axis long-exposure Strehl = sum_rho OTF_tel(rho) exp(-D_eps/2) / sum_rho OTF_tel(rho)

sources.supported_claim: C4 in VALIDATION.md: the directional sampler reproduces the anisoplanatic structure function along both baselines and the long-exposure Strehl of an ideally corrected multi-layer atmosphere.
applicability_limits: The paper's figures use Kolmogorov turbulence; the repository atmosphere is von Karman with L0 = 25 m, so the comparison uses the von Karman structure function in the same equations and reports the Kolmogorov values beside it rather than matching the paper's curves numerically.
The paper's observational test (Palomar binary) is not reproduced; no on-sky comparison is made here.
Ideal correction removes the on-axis phase of every layer exactly; the closed-loop 2.2 m demonstration is a different, finite-bandwidth case and is not compared with this model.
R1 Figure 2 is a 5 m telescope at 2.12 um (independent review); the 2.2 m, 1.65 um case here is compared with the same equations, not with that figure's values.

independent_review.access: relevant sections of the full text read in the independent review
confirmed: Section 2.1, Eqs. 3-5: OTF factorization neglecting cross terms with guide-star correction errors; the guide-star OTF is the diffraction reference under ideal on-axis correction

Section 2.2, Eqs. 8 and 12: shear s = h theta in metres at zenith; Eq. 12 contains two positive doubled terms and two negative displaced-baseline terms, the four-point form 2D(rho) + 2D(s) - D(rho + s) - D(rho - s)
Section 2.3, Figs. 1-2: Figure 1 illustrates the directional dependence; Figure 2 is a 5 m telescope, 2.12 um Strehl curve under ideal guide-star correction

sources.title: Anisoplanatism in adaptive optics
sources.venue: Journal of the Optical Society of America 72(1), 52-61
sources.access_status: not accessible during implementation (network policy); neither abstract nor full text read; a web-search snippet of the DOI page confirmed the volume, page and the definition of an isoplanatic patch angle theta_0 for high spatial frequencies and large apertures
locators_used: Isoplanatic angle theta_0 = [2.914 k^2 sec^(8/3)(zeta) int Cn^2(h) h^(5/3) dh]^(-3/5), here at zenith and in the equivalent form theta_0 = 0.314 r0(lambda) / hbar with hbar = (sum_l f_l h_l^(5/3))^(3/5)
Long-exposure anisoplanatic factor exp[-(theta/theta_0)^(5/3)], stated by the paper for the asymptotic regime of large apertures and high spatial frequencies

equation_as_used.theta0: theta_0 = 0.314 r0(lambda) / (sum_l f_l h_l^(5/3))^(3/5); 11.45 arcsec at 1.65 um for the robo_ao2_22m_ngs_draft@2 layer table

sources.supported_claim: Angular scaling reference only: in VALIDATION.md the factor is tabulated beside the finite-aperture OTF-integral Strehl to show that it is not sufficient to validate the 2.2 m curve (it includes piston and tilt of the differential phase and assumes the asymptotic regime).
applicability_limits: Asymptotic regime (aperture large compared with the layer displacements h theta); the 2.2 m aperture at 5-30 arcsec is not in it, so the factor is a bound-like reference, not a prediction to accept against.

independent_review.access: publisher abstract read in the independent review; full-text equations not used
confirmed: the exponential angular factor characterizes the imaging OTF at high spatial frequencies; the separate large-aperture statement concerns transmitter antenna gain; the abstract supplies no universal finite-aperture imaging Strehl acceptance test

repository_conventions.offset: ScienceOffset(x_arcsec, y_arcsec) relative to the on-axis guide star; theta_rad = arcsec * pi / 648000; positive x toward larger pupil x (array columns), positive y toward larger pupil y (array rows)
repository_conventions.sampling: layer l read at r + h_l theta - v_l t; shwfs_ao.backends.native.layered_atmosphere.LayeredFrozenFlowAtmosphere.directional_opd_at
repository_conventions.opd_vs_phase: the simulator stores OPD in metres; phase structure functions at the 500 nm reference wavelength are converted with (lambda_ref / 2 pi)^2, and to 1.65 um phase with (2 pi / lambda)^2
repository_conventions.psd_constant: 0.023 r0^(-5/3) (f^2 + L0^(-2))^(-11/6) two-sided; the closed-form structure function (exact constant 0.022896) is scaled by 0.023 / 0.022896
repository_conventions.strehl: shwfs_ao.science.metrics.peak_strehl_from_discrete_flux on unit-flux intensity images; long-exposure images are intensity means
